name: Sema MCP Bridge (kill the slash commands)
pitch: Replace pi-sema's 3 human slash commands and 4 hand-rolled static tools with a real bridge: spawn one long-lived `sema mcp` process and surface its tools (run_file/eval/docs/docs_search/fmt/check + notebook) as native Pi agent tools. Pi intentionally has no built-in MCP, so this bridge IS the sanctioned integration path.
mechanism: Extension spawns `sema mcp` as a stdio child (line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol 2024-11-05, only 4 methods: initialize/ping/tools/list/tools/call — sema-deftool-mcp report, server.rs:148-224; hand-rolling the client is ~150 lines, no @modelcontextprotocol/sdk needed). On session_start: initialize, tools/list, then for each tool `pi.registerTool()` with the MCP JSON schema translated to TypeBox and execute() forwarding to tools/call. registerTool mid-session auto-activates and rebuilds the system prompt (pi-sdk-types: loader.js:173-180 → agent-session.js:1782). Curate with `--include`/`--exclude` on the sema side (tools.rs:764-779) plus pi.registerFlag to pick tool subsets; use pi.setActiveTools to trim noisy tools per-turn (no unregisterTool exists, types.d.ts:893). Delete src/tools/* execSync wrappers and the 3 commands; keep the before_agent_start Sema knowledge injection.
risks: `sema mcp` hardcodes Sandbox::allow_all() (main.rs:921) — its eval tool is unsandboxed, so the bridge should carry promptGuidelines warning the model and optionally a tool_call hook gate. 17 default+notebook tools risk context bloat — mitigate with --exclude notebook/* by default. Client must re-list after evals since listChanged:false (see the upstream proposal).

name: /forge — Create-a-Tool flow (Claude Code /agents, but for deftools)
pitch: User types /forge "a tool that parses composer.lock and lists outdated deps" → the agent writes a Sema deftool, the extension verifies it in a strict sandbox, smoke-calls it, stores it in a known library dir, and registers it live. Mirrors Claude Code's 'Generate with Claude' agent-creation flow, with Voyager-style verification before storage.
mechanism: pi.registerCommand("forge") → ctx.ui.input for the description → pi.sendMessage({customType:"forge-request", content: authoring-prompt}, {triggerTurn:true}) so the main agent authors the deftool (prior-art: tool authoring wants the strongest model — Voyager GPT-3.5 ablation 5.7x). The agent submits via a `forge_submit` tool whose execute runs the verify pipeline: (1) `pi.exec("sema", ["eval","--stdin","--json","--sandbox","strict","--no-llm"])` — pi.exec's own timeout option is load-bearing because sema's --timeout flag is parsed but IGNORED (sema-deftool-mcp: main.rs:977 binds `timeout: _timeout`); (2) assert the JSON envelope {ok, error_msg, error_hint, error_line, error_col} and `(tool? name)`; (3) smoke-invoke the handler with sample args derived from the schema; on failure return the envelope diagnostics as the tool result so the model refines (Voyager ≤4 rounds; removing self-verification cost 73%). On pass: write `~/.sema/pi-tools/<name>.sema` (SEMA_HOME contract, home.rs:5-13), inject into the live `sema mcp` env via its eval tool, re-call tools/list (recomputed from env every call — empirically verified), and pi.registerTool the bridged tool. Record the creation with pi.appendEntry for session persistence.
risks: Strict sandbox denies LLM/network/shell/fs-write, so tools needing those caps can't be smoke-tested strictly — need a cap-escalation ui.confirm step. Verification of LLM-using tools needs FakeProvider/cassettes (sema-deftool-mcp §4) to avoid spend. Schema-derived sample args can be wrong; keep smoke-test failures advisory, envelope errors blocking.

name: Live Workflow Widget (journal-tailing sema_workflow_run tool)
pitch: A `sema_workflow_run` Pi tool that runs `sema workflow run` and renders live status — phase checklist, running agents, tool calls, token/cost budget — both inline in the transcript (streaming partials) and as a persistent widget above the editor. Never a bare spinner: the blocking node is always named (opencode issue #10802 is the cautionary tale).
mechanism: execute() spawns `sema workflow run <file> --args <json> --run-dir <dir>` via pi.exec with ctx.signal for Esc-cancellation; pin the run id with the SEMA_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID env seam (sema-workflows §1). Concurrently tail `<run-dir>/<id>/events.jsonl` — the journal is a FROZEN contract, one JSON line flushed per event, crash leaves a valid prefix (journal.rs:125-139), so fs.watch + line-buffered reads are safe on a live run; 1s poll fallback matches the official viewer. Parse the frozen vocabulary: run.started.phases[] gives the full declared plan up front (render pending checkboxes), phase.started/ended, agent.started/result correlated by agent_id (started-without-result = running), agent.tool_call, budget (tokens/cost_usd), run.ended. Render path A: onUpdate(partialResult) → tool_execution_update → renderResult({isPartial:true}) with ToolRenderContext.state reuse (types.d.ts:361-365, AC:322). Render path B: ctx.ui.setWidget("sema-wf", (tui,theme)=>Component) live panel, mutate state + tui.requestRender() (pi-sdk-types §1). Exit code 2 = needs-auth (main.rs:1345-1383, designed for orchestrator branching): parse auth.required events and ui.notify the exact `sema mcp login <url>` commands.
risks: No SSE/WebSocket or in-language event hook exists — tailing the file is the contract, but resume runs write separate events.resume-N.jsonl segments the tailer must merge. Per-leaf budget/tool-call attribution is documented best-effort under parallel fan-out (workflow.rs:540-547) — label concurrent sections approximately. run.started.code_version is emitted empty; read metadata.json instead.

name: Workflow Runs Overlay Dashboard
pitch: A ctrl+w overlay listing all workflow runs in the project (live and historical) with drill-down into a selected run's phase/agent tree — the Claude Code agent-view / opencode split-pane-subagents pattern, built on Pi's proven long-lived overlay support (DOOM runs at 35 FPS in one).
mechanism: pi.registerShortcut("ctrl+w") + pi.registerCommand("workflows") → ctx.ui.custom((tui,theme,keybindings,done)=>Component, {overlay:true, overlayOptions:{anchor:"top-right", width:"60%", maxHeight:"70%"}, onHandle}) (types.d.ts:116-126; overlay lifecycle per docs/tui.md:109-190). Left pane: run list by scanning `.sema/runs/*` newest-first by events.jsonl mtime (exactly what GET /api/runs does, workflow_view.rs:301) with status glyphs from result.json / absence-of-run.ended = live. Right pane: selected run's merged events.jsonl + events.resume-*.jsonl rendered as the viewer does — phases keyed by phase.started seq, agents attributed via phase_seq, correlated by agent_id (sema-workflows §2 nesting model). 1s re-poll of live journals; SelectList + handleInput for hjkl nav; OverlayHandle.setHidden to toggle without losing state; footer aggregate counter via ctx.ui.setStatus("wf", "2 running ⏳ 1 ✓") (prior-art distilled pattern #1). Skip the SQLite index.db (avoids a native dep) — parse JSONL directly; optionally shell `sqlite3 -json` via pi.exec for the cross-run summary.
risks: Components are disposed on overlay close — must recreate, not reuse (docs/tui.md:166-188). Overlay is TUI-mode only (ctx.mode guard); RPC mode needs the widget fallback. Large journals need capped tail-reads (events already cap prompt/output fields, so line sizes are bounded).

name: create_sema_tool — the self-extending loop
pitch: The big one: a meta-tool the AGENT calls autonomously mid-task — 'I need a tool that X' → it writes a deftool, the extension verifies it sandboxed, injects it into the shared sema process, and registers it as a Pi tool it can call on the very next turn. This is the full Voyager loop inside one Pi session; no restart, no /reload, no human in the loop except an approval gate.
mechanism: pi.registerTool("create_sema_tool") with params {name, description, source, sample_args?}. execute(): (1) verify via `pi.exec("sema", ["eval","--stdin","--json","--sandbox","strict","--no-llm"], {timeout})` asserting the JSON envelope + `(tool? name)` + optional smoke call — external timeout mandatory (sema --timeout is a no-op); on failure return error_msg/error_hint/error_line to the model for refinement; (2) ui.confirm approval gate showing the source (deterministic gate around a probabilistic author — prior-art distillation #5; gptel-confirm pattern); (3) inject the source into the ONE long-lived `sema mcp` process via its eval tool — deftool env.set()s into the shared global env (special_forms.rs:70-135) and the next tools/list picks it up because the list is recomputed from iter_bindings every call (tools.rs:558, empirically verified: dyn-add appeared and returned 42); (4) persist to ~/.sema/pi-tools/<name>.sema; (5) pi.registerTool the bridged Pi tool — registerTool is callable at any time including from inside another tool's execute (loader.js Map.set + runtime.refreshTools(); only guard is runtime.assertActive), auto-activates and rebuilds the system prompt so the agent can call it next turn. promptGuidelines on the meta-tool teach the model when to forge vs. use bash.
risks: The verified artifact runs sandboxed but the INVOCATION path (sema mcp) is unsandboxed (Sandbox::allow_all hardcoded) — verification proves absence of syntax/logic errors, not safety; the ui.confirm gate plus optionally a tool_call hook signature-pin (GenAIScript rug-pull defense, prior-art §5) is the mitigation. Name collisions with built-ins: across-extension 'first registration wins', within-extension last-wins — prefix generated tools (Amp's tb__ pattern). Runaway self-extension bloats the tool list — cap active generated tools via setActiveTools.

name: Tool Library with lazy proxy (progressive disclosure)
pitch: Forged tools accumulate in ~/.sema/pi-tools/ and load every session — but instead of dumping N tools into context, expose one ~200-token `sema_tool` proxy with search/invoke, the exact design that made pi-mcp-adapter the #1 Pi package (129K dl/mo) and that the MCP ecosystem converged on (Stainless dynamic mode).
mechanism: On session_start, spawn `sema mcp ~/.sema/pi-tools/*.sema .pi/sema-tools/*.sema` — filepath mode evaluates the files and exposes every non-private deftool (main.rs:926-950; hide helpers with _-prefix or :mcp/expose #f). Register ONE Pi tool `sema_tool` with params {search?: string, tool?: string, args?: object}: search filters the cached tools/list by name+description substring/fuzzy; invoke forwards to tools/call with json_args_to_sema's named→positional mapping doing coercion server-side (tools.rs:322). Hot/frequent tools get promoted to direct pi.registerTool registrations via a settings flag (pi-mcp-adapter's directTools pattern). Library becomes durable/shareable via `sema pkg init/publish` to pkg.sema-lang.com (sema-deftool-mcp §3) — a Pi-installable package of verified tools, smolagents push_to_hub style. Project-local .pi/sema-tools/ layered over global, Claude-Code-skills-style tiering.
risks: Proxy indirection costs the model one extra call (search then invoke) — acceptable per pi-mcp-adapter's adoption, but description quality determines routing accuracy (Claude Code skills lesson). Substring search degrades past ~50 tools; embedding retrieval (Voyager top-5) is the upgrade path but needs an embedding dep. Restart-loaded only — pair with create_sema_tool for in-session additions.

name: Deterministic .sema write gate (workflow/tool linting hook)
pitch: Every time the agent writes or edits a .sema file containing defworkflow, a tool_call hook runs `sema workflow check --strict --json` and blocks the write with the diagnostics fed back to the model — Claude Code's exit-2 hook protocol, implemented with Pi's native blocking events. Zero LLM cost, catches E-WF-SHAPE/W-STEP-AGENT-TOOLS/etc. before the file ever hits disk wrong.
mechanism: pi.on("tool_call") with isToolCallEventType("write"/"edit") narrowing (types.d.ts:619-661, 730-740); if the target path ends .sema and content matches /\(defworkflow/, write proposed content to the scratchpad, run `pi.exec("sema", ["workflow","check",tmp,"--strict","--json"])` — static validation, no eval/LLM (main.rs:548-624; full diagnostic code list in workflow_check.rs) — and on errors return {block:true, reason: formatted diagnostics} so stderr-equivalent feedback reaches the model (prior-art: Claude Code hooks exit 2 = block + stderr fed to model). For non-workflow .sema files fall back to a parse-only `sema eval --sandbox strict` of `(read-many ...)` or `sema fmt --check`. Warnings (W-*) pass through as an appended note via tool_result patching rather than blocking.
risks: workflow check's checks only fire inside defworkflow bodies — plain deftool files get weaker parse-only validation. Blocking on W-level diagnostics would cause loops; block only on E-level. Adds ~50-100ms exec per .sema write (negligible).

name: Sema subagents: defagent as budgeted, journaled delegation
pitch: Pi intentionally ships no sub-agents; give it Sema-native ones. A `sema_agent` tool runs a stored defagent wrapped in a one-step defworkflow, which buys journaling, resume memoization, and hard cost caps for free — and plugs straight into the workflow widget for live status.
mechanism: Library defagents in ~/.sema/pi-tools/agents/*.sema (defagent = VM special form, Agent{name,system,tools,max_turns,model}, value.rs:435-442). pi.registerTool("sema_agent") {agent, prompt, max_usd?}: execute generates a wrapper `(defworkflow pi-delegate "..." {:budget {:usd max_usd}} (step prompt {:agent A :name (agent/name A)}))` and runs it via `sema workflow run` under pi.exec — step {:agent} routes through agent/run with the agent's own tools/model, journaling every agent.tool_call via the :on-tool-call shim (prelude.rs:465-470), and the sticky over_budget latch forces {:status :failed "budget exceeded"} at step entry (context.rs:63-76). Reuse the Live Workflow Widget tailer for the running-agent panel (prior-art: opencode's missing subagent visibility is the #1 requested TUI feature, issues 15223/15363). Return result.json's envelope as the tool result; failed runs are --resume-able for free replay of memoized leaves. Parallel delegation = one defworkflow with (parallel [...] n) fan-out, bounded at 8.
risks: The sema process needs its own LLM keys/config (llm/auto-configure) — spend happens outside Pi's accounting; surface the budget events in the widget to compensate. USD caps are pricing-table best-effort. No mid-run cancellation primitive in sema (WF-1 deferred) — pi.exec kill via ctx.signal is the abort path, which orphans the run as failed-by-crash (journal stays valid).

name: Skill + prompt export via resources_discover
pitch: Every stored tool/workflow also generates a SKILL.md and a prompt template, wired in through pi-sema's currently-empty resources_discover stub — giving ~100-token progressive disclosure in the system prompt, /skill:name invocation, and /run-<workflow> slash commands with $ARGUMENTS substitution.
mechanism: src/hooks/resources.ts today returns empty arrays (pi-sdk-types: current-usage). Change: on resources_discover (fires after session_start, reason startup|reload — types.d.ts:393-403), scan the tool library, generate `<cache>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (frontmatter name+description from tool/description; body = schema table + usage examples; Agent Skills standard per agentskills.io, which Pi implements leniently — pi-docs-web §3) and `<cache>/prompts/run-<workflow>.md` templates embedding `sema workflow run <file> --args $ARGUMENTS`, then return {skillPaths, promptPaths}. After create_sema_tool stores a new tool, regenerate and use the documented reload_runtime pattern (examples/extensions/reload-runtime.ts: a tool queues /reload-runtime → ctx.reload() → resources_discover refires with reason "reload") so new skills index without restart — the same file-watch-equivalent hot path Claude Code skills use (prior-art §1).
risks: ctx.reload() tears down and rebinds the whole extension runtime — the bridge's sema mcp child must be reconnected in the new session_start (persist injected-tool state by re-evaling library files, which is idempotent since deftool just env.set()s). Skill routing accuracy depends on generated description quality.

name: Hygiene: pi.exec migration + streaming tool renderers
pitch: Quick win independent of everything else: replace src/sema.ts's node execSync + hand-rolled quoting/timeout with pi.exec, and give the remaining tools onUpdate streaming, renderResult, and promptSnippet/promptGuidelines. Foundation work — every other proposal builds on pi.exec's AbortSignal semantics.
mechanism: pi.exec(command, args, {signal: ctx.signal, timeout, cwd}) → {stdout, stderr, code, killed} (dist/core/exec.d.ts, types.d.ts:887) replaces execSync — array args kill the quoting bugs, ctx.signal inherits Esc-cancellation, killed flag distinguishes timeout from failure. For sema_build/long evals, stream stderr progress via onUpdate(partial) → renderResult({isPartial:true}) (types.d.ts:361-365). Add promptSnippet one-liners and promptGuidelines bullets so the tools are self-documenting in the system prompt (dynamic-tools.ts example shows both). Keep sema_eval but have it pass --json and surface the structured envelope (error_line/error_col/error_hint) instead of raw text.
risks: Essentially none; behavior-preserving. Only note: pi.exec is unavailable outside the extension API surface, so any shared helper must take the pi handle.

name: Upstream: listChanged push notifications (completes the loop with zero polling)
pitch: A single-file change in sema's server.rs — flip capabilities.tools.listChanged to true and emit notifications/tools/list_changed after any eval/run_file that binds a ToolDef — turns the de-facto-dynamic tool list into a spec-compliant push-dynamic one. We control both ends, so the patchy-client-support problem that plagues the MCP ecosystem doesn't apply.
mechanism: Sema side: server.rs:165-176 currently reports {tools:{listChanged:false}} and never notifies, but the list is already recomputed from the live env on every tools/list (tools.rs:558) and the stdout write half is available in the request loop — the research report calls this out as a small change: detect new ToolDef bindings after eval/run_file (diff iter_bindings count or snapshot names) and write the {"method":"notifications/tools/list_changed"} line (MCP spec 2025-06-18 sanctions exactly this — prior-art §5). Pi side: the bridge's stdio reader dispatches the notification → re-call tools/list → diff → pi.registerTool new entries / setActiveTools to drop removed ones. Until upstream lands, the bridge falls back to re-listing after every eval/run_file/create_sema_tool call it itself initiated (covers 100% of self-extension traffic; misses only out-of-band mutations).
risks: Upstream dependency: needs a sema-mcp crate change + release (currently 1.30.0); the workaround (re-list after self-initiated calls) is fully adequate for the self-extending loop, so this is an elegance upgrade, not a blocker. Guard against notification storms when a run_file registers many tools (debounce one notification per request).
